meanings.note: Placed directly before an indefinite noun without ال- to mean 'the last' (آخر يوم 'the last day', آخر الساحة 'the far end of the courtyard').

examples.trans: The attic room is at the end of the floor.
Today is the last day of the week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعطي, بيعطي).

examples.trans: Did the shopkeeper give you a receipt?
Give me the breakfast bag, please.

meanings.note: Used to express certainty or agreement.

examples.trans: I will certainly come to the party.

examples.text: أكيد ما رح أنسى أجبلك الكتاب بكرة الصبح.
examples.trans: For sure I won't forget to bring you the book tomorrow morning.

meanings.note: Conjunction 'or' in statements and open questions.

examples.text: مكتوب عليها اسم أو رقم تليفون؟
examples.trans: Is there a name or phone number written on it?
We need two or three minutes.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: Can mean a business card, playing card, or SIM/recharge card.

examples.trans: Do you have my card?

examples.text: شحنت الكرت تبع الباص عند السوبرماركت الصبح.
examples.trans: I topped up the bus card at the supermarket this morning.

meanings.note: Form VIII geminate verb.

examples.text: الورق القديم امتص ريحة العسل والبرتقال.
examples.trans: The old paper absorbed the scent of honey and orange.
The blotter absorbs excess ink quickly.

meanings.note: Signature Jordanian/Palestinian pronunciation (with z) of بالضبط ('exactly!').

examples.trans: Exactly! You have become one of us.
Tell me exactly what to buy.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: برتقالات.

examples.trans: The fresh orange juice is cold.
We bought oranges and apples from the market.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببرد, بيبرد).

examples.trans: The cake is cooling on the rack right now.
The radiator is starting to get cold at the bottom.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of برش ('to grate'). Used in baking for citrus zest (برش البرتقال 'orange zest', برش الليمون 'lemon zest').

examples.text: برش البرتقال بيعطي الكيكة ريحة حلوة.
examples.trans: Orange zest gives the cake a lovely aroma.
We added one teaspoon of lemon zest.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: Means 'after' (بعد المطر) and with a future span 'in' (بعد أربعين دقيقة 'in forty minutes').

examples.trans: He arrives in forty minutes.
How lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: The musical instrument.

examples.trans: He plays the piano every day.
The black piano is placed in the corner of the parlour.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتحرك, بيتحرك).

examples.text: في قطعة معدن تحركت جوا الصندوق!
examples.trans: A piece of metal shifted inside the box!
The car pulled away from the door.

meanings.note: The standalone form of the number 3.

examples.trans: Count to ten: one, two, three.

examples.text: رتبنا الصحون واحد تنين تلاتة عالطاولة.
examples.trans: We lined up the plates one, two, three on the table.

meanings.note: The number 30.

examples.trans: His age is now thirty years.

examples.text: ضلينا تلاتين دقيقة بنستنى الكيكة تبرد.
examples.trans: We spent thirty minutes waiting for the cake to cool.

meanings.note: Form II verbal noun of لمّع ('to polish wood, brass, or shoes').

examples.text: بقي بس تلميع دواسات النحاس بقماشة ناعمة.
examples.trans: All that's left is polishing the brass pedals with a soft cloth.

examples.text: بعد التلميع رجع خشب الجوز يلمع زي المراية.
examples.trans: After polishing, the walnut wood shone like a mirror again.

meanings.note: Form V verb from نفس ('breath').

examples.text: فتحت الشباك عشان أتنفس هوا نضيف.
examples.trans: I opened the window to breathe fresh air.

examples.text: بعد ما رتبنا القائمة، قدرت أتنفس براحة.
examples.trans: Once we organized the list, I could breathe easily.

meanings.note: Collective masculine noun for berries/mulberries (singulative توتة 'one berry').

examples.trans: The berry and almond cake turned out delicious!
We have an old mulberry tree in the neighbourhood.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of جنّ; often used hyperbolically in speech for something absurd or crazy.

examples.text: نترك الكيكة تبرد واحنا بنشم ورق؟ هادا جنون!
examples.trans: Leave the cake to cool while we smell paper? That is madness!

examples.text: السواقة بهالزحمة بدون صبر جنون رسمي.
examples.trans: Driving in this traffic without patience is pure madness.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بجهز, بيجهز).

examples.trans: We prepared the quiet attic room for you.
Salma got breakfast ready early.

meanings.note: Standard word for a stone or rock, singular form.

examples.trans: We found a strange stone in the garden.

examples.text: لقينا حجر منحوت عليه نجمة صغيرة.
examples.trans: We found a stone with a small star carved on it.

meanings.note: Standard and Jordanian feminine noun for a public park or walled garden (حدائق 'parks').

examples.trans: The park bench is painted beside the arch.

examples.text: بنتمشى بالحديقة كل يوم جمعة العصر.
examples.trans: We walk in the park every Friday afternoon.

meanings.note: Used in معك حق ('you are right / you have a point').

examples.trans: You are right, the weather is cold today.
Everyone has a right to rest.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: حقيقية, plural: حقيقيين).

examples.trans: Did you book the room under your real name?
Let me show you my real work.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to speak, talk, tell' (بحكي / حكى).

examples.trans: Salma chats with all the neighbours.
Tell me everything I need to know.

meanings.note: One of the most frequently used adjectives in Jordanian Arabic to mean beautiful, sweet, nice, or good.

examples.trans: This dress is very beautiful on you.

examples.text: طعم العسل مع قشر البرتقال حلو ومتوازن.
examples.trans: The taste of honey with orange peel is sweet and balanced.

meanings.note: Form I verb; often describes honey, milk, or dough turning sour.

examples.text: العسل الدافي بضل طري بدون ما يحمض.
examples.trans: Warm honey stays soft without turning sour.

examples.text: إذا تركتي الحليب برا التلاجة رح يحمض.
examples.trans: If you leave the milk outside the fridge it will go sour.

meanings.note: Very frequent Jordanian verb: خليني ('let me'), خلينا ('let us'), خليك ('stay!'), خلي ('keep/leave').

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
Hot bread makes people pleasant!

meanings.note: The number five, used in counting abstractly or before masculine counted nouns.

examples.trans: I bought five books today.

examples.text: عندنا خمسة أبواب خشب بتطلع عالحديقة.
examples.trans: We have five wooden doors leading out to the garden.

meanings.note: Used to describe warm weather, warm water, or a cozy feeling.

examples.trans: The weather today is very warm.

examples.text: الحليب الدافي بسكر الخميرة وبخليها تتفاعل.
examples.trans: Warm milk activates the yeast and helps it rise.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: دقايق.

examples.trans: I will be back in ten minutes on the dot.
Wait one minute, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for painting walls, shutters, or wooden furniture (noun دهان 'paint').

examples.text: رح ندهن الشيش باللون الأخضر يوم التنين.
examples.trans: We are going to paint the shutters green on Monday.

examples.text: دهنا الكراسي الخشب وتركناها تنشف بالشمس.
examples.trans: We painted the wooden chairs and left them to dry in the sun.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from ذهب (gold); also pronounced دهبي in everyday Jordanian.

examples.text: اخبزي الكيكة ليصير لونها ذهبي حلو.
examples.trans: Bake the cake until its colour turns a lovely golden.
She won a gold medal in the cooking competition.

meanings.note: Common everyday verb for 'went' in the past tense. Also used as a future particle.

examples.trans: He went to work in the morning.

examples.text: رامي راح عالمكتبة يدور على الكتاب القديم.
examples.trans: Rami went to the library to look for the old book.

رجع.gloss: to return; come back; start again

meanings.en: to return; come back; start again
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برجع, بيرجع).

examples.trans: Can you run there and come back in ten minutes?
Did the pipe start dripping again?

meanings.note: Future tense marker in Jordanian and Levantine Arabic, equivalent to 'sa-' in MSA.

examples.trans: I will travel tomorrow.

examples.text: رح نذوق التلات كيكات بعد ما يبردوا شوي.
examples.trans: We will taste the three cakes after they cool a little.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: رسمية, plural: رسميين).

examples.trans: Save the formal talk for the guests only!
An official letter arrived in the noon post.

meanings.note: Geminate verb used for splashing water or sprinkling herbs/sugar.

examples.trans: I sprinkled a little water on the flowers in the morning.

examples.text: سلمى رشت قرفة مطحونة فوق الكيكة.
examples.trans: Salma dusted ground cinnamon over the cake.

meanings.note: Feminine noun from رقيق ('thin'). Broken plural رقائق refers to flakes (such as toasted almond flakes) or thin wafers.

examples.trans: We sprinkled toasted almond flakes on top.

examples.text: رقاقة العجين لازم تكون رفيعة كتير.
examples.trans: The dough sheet has to be very thin.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a number, digit, or phone number.

examples.trans: What is your phone number?

examples.text: كل بطاقة إلها رقم متسلسل من واحد لعشرة.
examples.trans: Each card has a serial number from one to ten.

meanings.note: Refers to a corner of a room or street, or a geometric angle.

examples.trans: Put the chair in the corner.
The chest is placed in the northern corner of the room.

meanings.note: Usually implies olive oil in Jordan unless specified otherwise, but used for all oils.

examples.trans: Put oil and thyme on the bread.

examples.text: دهنا القالب بشوية زيت زيتون نضيف.
examples.trans: We greased the pan with a little clean olive oil.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a year.

examples.trans: This car is this year's model.

examples.text: مرّت سنة كاملة على آخر زيارة للمزرعة.
examples.trans: A whole year has passed since the last visit to the farm.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Names both wooden shutter slats/louvres and thin slices of bread or lemon.

examples.text: دهنا شرائح الشيش الخشب وحدة ورا التانية.
examples.trans: We painted the wooden shutter slats one after another.

examples.text: حطينا شريحة ليمون رقيقة بجانب كاسة الشاي.
examples.trans: We placed a thin slice of lemon beside the tea glass.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشم, بيشم).

examples.trans: Smell that wonderful aroma in the kitchen!
We smelled the cinnamon from the stairs.

meanings.note: Feminine imperative of شمّ (to smell), addressing Salma.

examples.text: شمّي ريحة القرفة والهيل طالعة من الفرن!
examples.trans: Smell the scent of cinnamon and cardamom coming out of the oven!

examples.text: بحب أشمّ هوا نضيف بالحديقة الصبح.
examples.trans: I love breathing in fresh air in the garden in the morning.

meanings.note: Used across modern Jordanian kitchens and cafés for both male and female head chefs.

examples.text: الدفتر جاهز يا شيف سلمى، بشو نبلش؟
examples.trans: The clipboard is ready, Chef Salma—what do we start with?

examples.text: الشيف ذاق الشوربة وابتسم من أول معلقة.
examples.trans: The chef tasted the soup and smiled from the very first spoonful.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشبك, بيشبك).

examples.trans: Plug in Tariq's brass lamp.
We clipped the second sheet to the envelope.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصير, بيصير).

examples.trans: You became one of us quickly!
Did the water upstairs turn cold?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: صفحات.

examples.trans: Read the second page of the letter.
The notebook fell open to the middle page.

meanings.note: The season of summer.

examples.trans: Summer in Jordan is usually hot.

examples.text: بالصيف بنحب نقعد بالعريشة تحت العنب.
examples.trans: In the summer we like to sit under the grape arbour.

meanings.note: Broken plural صواني ('serving trays' or 'oven baking pans').

examples.text: جهزنا تلات صواني خبز عشان تدخل الفرن الفجر.
examples.trans: We prepped three trays of bread to go into the oven at dawn.

examples.text: نور حملت صينية الشاي بالنعنع للساحة.
examples.trans: Nour carried the mint tea tray out to the courtyard.

meanings.note: Very common Levantine verb meaning to stay, remain, or keep doing something.

examples.trans: He stayed at home and didn't go out.

examples.text: ضل الدفتر مفتوح عالطاولة طول الليل.
examples.trans: The notebook remained open on the table all night.

meanings.note: Used for a coat of paint (طبقة دهان), a layer of pastry, or a building storey.

examples.text: الطبقة الأولى نشفت وصارت جاهزة للطبقة التانية.
examples.trans: The first coat has dried and is ready for the second coat.

examples.text: دهان المي بيكفيه طبقتين رقيقتين عشان يطلع ناعم.
examples.trans: Water-based paint only needs two thin coats to come out smooth.

meanings.note: Everyday food adjective for soft, tender bread or fresh dough.

examples.text: الخبز الطالع من الفرن لسه سخن وطري كتير.
examples.trans: The bread coming out of the oven is still hot and very soft.

examples.text: اعجن العجينة منيح لحد ما تصير طرية ومتماسكة.
examples.trans: Knead the dough well until it becomes soft and cohesive.

meanings.note: Intensive fa''aal adjective from طار (to fly); in chemistry and cooking describes volatile aromatic oils or fleeting notes.

examples.text: عطر قشر الليمون طيار وبروح بسرعة بالحرارة.
examples.trans: The scent of lemon zest is volatile and fades quickly with heat.

examples.text: هادا النوع من العطور خفيف وطيار.
examples.trans: This kind of essence is light and volatile.

meanings.note: Plural of عزيز ('dear'), standard in Arabic letters and postcards.

examples.trans: Welcome, my dear friends—you've lit up the place!

examples.text: أخوي الصغير عزيز على قلبي كتير.
examples.trans: My little brother is very dear to my heart.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Here is mint tea with honey.
Mountain honey tastes wonderful.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'on', 'upon', or 'to'.

examples.trans: The book is on the table.

examples.text: حطينا الخريطة على الطاولة وبلشنا نحللها.
examples.trans: We laid the map on the table and began analysing it.

meanings.note: Levantine progressive marker placed before a present-tense verb to show action happening right now.

examples.trans: The water is flowing inside the pipe right now!

examples.text: كنت عم بدور على دفتري هلا.
examples.trans: I was just looking for my notebook.

meanings.note: Means 'about' (عن الزبدة), 'off / away from' (عن جبيني), and appears in عن جد ('really!') and عن إذنك ('excuse me').

examples.trans: I will carry the suitcase up for you.
I heard your voices about the butter!

meanings.note: Feminine noun; also used in the delighted Jordanian exclamation يا عيني! ('oh my! / how lovely!').

examples.trans: Close your eyes and smell the coffee!
Oh my, look at that warm light in the courtyard!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بغمض, بيغمض).

examples.trans: Close your eyes and taste the cake!
She closed her eyes and listened to the rain.

meanings.note: After negation, ما ... غير means 'only / nothing except'.

examples.text: ما معي غير المعطف اللي علي!
examples.trans: I have nothing with me except the coat I have on!
There are only two valves on the shelf.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أفران.

examples.text: لفائف القرفة طلعت من الفرن هلا.
examples.trans: The cinnamon rolls just came out of the oven.
The bakery down the street bakes in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قاسية, plural: قاسيين).

examples.text: كان يعمل حاله قاسي خمس ثواني بس!
examples.trans: He used to act tough for just five seconds!
Amman's winter cold is sometimes harsh.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قديمة, plural: قدام).

examples.trans: The courtyard has an old jasmine tree.
The old hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Collective noun for fruit peels, citrus zest, or eggshells; single piece is قشرة.

examples.text: بشرنا قشر الليمون فوق خليط الكيكة.
examples.trans: We grated the lemon peel over the cake batter.

examples.text: قشر البرتقال المطبوخ بعطي نكهة غنية بالعسل.
examples.trans: Cooked orange peel gives a rich flavour with honey.

meanings.note: Past tense of 'to be' for 3rd person masculine singular. Widely used as an auxiliary verb.

examples.trans: The weather was cold yesterday.

examples.text: الطعم كان متوازن كتير بين العسل والليمون.
examples.trans: The flavour was very well balanced between the honey and lemon.

meanings.note: Masculine noun; plural كتب (kutub), written like the verb كتب 'he wrote' (katab) but said differently.

examples.trans: This book is about the history of Amman.
I put the books on the shelf.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بكشر, بيكشر).

examples.text: لما يغلط بالنغمة كان يكشر عالحيط!
examples.trans: When he missed a note, he used to scowl at the wall!
Do not frown, smile!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: كلمات.

examples.trans: She did not say a single word to anyone.
The word thank you warms the heart.

meanings.note: Refers to a single, whole cake, or a distinct slice (singulative form of kēk).

examples.trans: I made a delicious chocolate cake.

examples.text: كيكة التوت اللي عملتها سلمى طلعت خفيفة وهشة.
examples.trans: The berry cake that Salma made turned out light and fluffy.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'no' or 'not', used exactly like Standard Arabic.

examples.trans: No, I don't want to go today.

examples.text: لا تنسوا تطفيوا الفرن بعد ما تخلصوا الخبيز.
examples.trans: Do not forget to turn off the oven after you finish baking.

meanings.note: Very common Jordanian word to indicate that an action is ongoing or hasn't happened yet.

examples.trans: I still haven't finished my work.

examples.text: الكيكة لسا بالفرن وبدها كمان خمس دقايق.
examples.trans: The cake is still in the oven and needs five more minutes.

meanings.note: Core word in إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again / goodbye!') and also 'reunion / meeting'.

examples.trans: Goodbye, have a pleasant trip!

examples.text: كان لقاء دافي بعد غياب طويل.
examples.trans: It was a warm reunion after a long absence.

meanings.en: to shine; to gleam; to sparkle
meanings.note: Sound Form I verb (بلمع / لمعت) from root ل-م-ع, used for polished metal or bright ink.

examples.trans: The drawings still shine on the paper.
The brass lock gleamed in the sun.

meanings.note: Literally means almonds, but heavily used in Jordanian youth slang to mean 'everything is perfect' or 'great'.

examples.trans: The situation is perfect, don't worry.

examples.text: زينت سلمى وش الكيكة بشرايح لوز محمص.
examples.trans: Salma decorated the top of the cake with toasted almond slices.

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: I haven't eaten anything since the morning.

examples.text: ما عرفت إنه العلبة فيها طابق سري من تحت.
examples.trans: I did not know that the box had a secret compartment underneath.

meanings.note: Passive participle of برش (to grate); very common in recipes for grated lemon zest, cheese, or coconut.

examples.text: حطينا قشر برتقال مبروش فوق الكيكة.
examples.trans: We put grated orange zest on top of the cake.
Grated cheese melts quickly in the oven.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine form of مثل ('like, similar to').

examples.trans: Its color is dark blue like your suitcase!
The water is cold as ice.

meanings.note: Passive participle indicating that an object has been set down or positioned somewhere.

examples.trans: The key is placed on the table.

examples.text: المرطبان الدهبي محطوط على أعلى رف بالمطبخ.
examples.trans: The golden jar is placed on the highest shelf in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian noun for any retail shop or spot (pl. محلات).

examples.trans: Below is the signature of the antique shop.
There's a pastry shop next to the house.

meanings.note: Form II passive participle from حمّص ('to toast/roast'): describes nuts, coffee, or bread.

examples.trans: Toasted walnuts give a nice crunch.

examples.text: شوية لوز محمص فوق الرز كتير زاكي.
examples.trans: A few toasted almonds on top of the rice are delicious.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مدد.

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
He travelled for two weeks in summer.

meanings.note: The most common negation particle in Levantine Arabic for non-verbs.

examples.trans: I am not upset with you.

examples.text: هادا المفتاح مش للباب الرئيسي، هادا للخزانة.
examples.trans: This key is not for the main door; this one is for the cupboard.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine metathesis of ملعقة ('spoon'), placing the ع before the ل.

examples.text: حطّي معلقة صغيرة قرفة على وجه السحلب.
examples.trans: Put a teaspoon of cinnamon on top of the sahlab.

examples.text: نسيت أجيب المعلقة عشان أحرك الشاي فيها.
examples.trans: I forgot to bring the spoon to stir the tea with.

meanings.note: Form II participle adjective (feminine مغبرة, plural مغبرين) from غبرة ('dust').

examples.text: الدرابزين كان مغبر قبل ما نمسحه.
examples.trans: The railing was dusty before we wiped it.
The old boxes in the storeroom are all dusty.

meanings.note: Noun of place from ق-ع-د ('to sit'); names the seat of a chair or a garden bench.

examples.text: ارفع مقعد الكرسي شوي عشان يطوي معك.
examples.trans: Lift the chair seat slightly so it folds for you.

examples.text: في مقعد خشب طويل تحت شجرة الساحة.
examples.trans: There is a long wooden bench under the courtyard tree.

meanings.note: Form II passive participle of لطّخ (to smear/stain); describes ink, paint, or jam stains.

examples.text: الحبر كان ملطخ على الزاوية التحتانية للورقة.
examples.trans: The ink was smudged on the bottom corner of the sheet.

examples.text: إيديه ملطخة بعجين وطحين من الخبيز.
examples.trans: His hands are smeared with dough and flour from baking.

meanings.note: Very common word of approval or rating something highly.

examples.trans: Your work is excellent today.

examples.text: توازن السكر والليمون بهاي الكيكة ممتاز جدا.
examples.trans: The balance of sugar and lemon in this cake is truly excellent.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am from Jordan.

examples.text: جبنا العسل البلدي الصافي من مزرعة قريبة.
examples.trans: We brought the pure local honey from a nearby farm.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian pronunciation (often نعنع in rapid speech) for fresh or dried mint added to tea.

examples.text: قطفنا شوية نعناع أخضر عشان الشاي.
examples.trans: We picked some fresh mint for the tea.
The dried mint in the jar has a strong aroma.

meanings.note: Key culinary term in baking and tasting notes; plural نكهات.

examples.text: في نكهة قرفة خفيفة بطرف الكيكة.
examples.trans: There is a light cinnamon flavour at the edge of the cake.

examples.text: كل صينية جربت نكهة عسل مختلفة.
examples.trans: Each tin tried a different honey flavour.

meanings.note: Everyday demonstrative pronoun for masculine singular objects.

examples.trans: This boy is very smart.

examples.text: هاد المحل ببيع أطيب كنافة نابلسية بعمان.
examples.trans: This shop sells the best Nabulsi kunafa in Amman.

meanings.note: Signature urban Jordanian/Levantine adverb for now (also spelled هلا in Jordan).

examples.text: هلق رح نفتح الصينية ونذوق أول قطعة.
examples.trans: Right now we will open the tin and taste the first piece.
We finished writing the notes just now.

meanings.note: Third person masculine pronoun.

examples.trans: He is the one who said so.

examples.text: طارق هو اللي اقترح نطلع رحلة على البترا.
examples.trans: Tareq is the one who suggested we take a trip to Petra.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun; وجه لوجه means 'face to face'. Plural: وجوه.

examples.trans: They stood face to face under the tree.
The top of the cake turned golden in the oven.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ورشات.

examples.trans: There is a brass lamp in my workshop downstairs.
The old bag is from my grandfather's workshop.

meanings.note: Collective noun used for paper material or leaves of a tree.

examples.text: جيب لي شوية ورق أكتب عليهم.
examples.trans: Bring me some paper to write on.

examples.text: لفينا ورق دوالي اليوم الصبح للغدا مع اللبن.
examples.trans: We rolled grape leaves this morning for lunch with yogurt.

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Oh Ahmed, come here.

examples.text: يا سيدي، تفضل اشرب معنا فنجان قهوة قبل ما تروح.
examples.trans: Sir, please come have a cup of coffee with us before you leave.
